newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil prison rebellion enters sixth day.
newsitem.headline: Brazil prison rebellion enters sixth day.

text.p: About 15 Brazilian prisoners who revolted and seized nine hostages after their escape bid was foiled five days ago were showing no signs of ending their uprising, military police said on Thursday.
"To live locked up is not to live. It's better to die," local Globo television quoted the group's leader as telling his wife after listening impassively to her recorded pleas to surrender.
But the group released a female hostage late on Wednesday night who was shown on television being lowered by ropes to freedom over the prison wall, in Vitoria da Conquista in Bahia state.

"The hostage was pushed out into the exercise area and then we lifted her over the wall. She was very upset because of the trauma of her ordeal but otherwise she is in good health," a local military police officer said.
Two evangelical priests and one woman are among the eight remaining hostages still being held. The remainder are prison workers.
Around 50 other prisoners who did not take part in the rebellion are also trapped in the prison's exercise ground, unable to leave through the area occupied by the rebels and the hostages.
The rebels are demanding four cars, revolvers and around $3,800 but the police are refusing to supply the guns or ammunition, the police officer said.
Food and other necessities were being lowered over the walls into the exercise area using ropes, he said.
A police official said the rebellious prisoners seized their hostages during visiting hours on Saturday after authorities discovered a tunnel they had dug to try and escape.
